end.summary:
Anika understood that objects with curved surfaces roll, using examples such as a ball, bottle and drum.
Anika practised that the same object can roll one way and stand or stack another way; this is still not steady and needs checking next time.
Anika practised that flat tops and bottoms stack; easy questions were right, but a why or new-situation question is still to be checked.
They used shape and position clues when discussing balls, boxes, glasses, plates and containers.
end.parentNote: Anika practised sorting objects by curved and flat surfaces. They used shape and position clues to explain why a ball, bottle and drum could roll, and why a box or plate could stand or stack. The difference between an object rolling on one side and standing on another still needs more practice; ask, “Why would it roll or stack?” with new household objects such as a cup, box and tin.
